root_cause: The navigation controller sets aria-activedescendant to the option's data-value (the label) instead of the option's ID, causing assistive technologies to receive incorrect active descendant information.
repair_strategy: Replace the assignment of aria-activedescendant with the option element's ID (list[currentFocus].id) so that it correctly references the active option element.
expected_accessibility_effect: aria-activedescendant will now reference the correct option element ID, enabling screen readers to accurately announce the active suggestion as users navigate with ArrowUp/ArrowDown.
functional_risks: No functional impact expected; the change only affects an accessibility attribute. Data selection and onSelection callbacks remain unchanged because they rely on the data object, not the attribute.
verification_requirements: After typing 'ma' and pressing ArrowDown, the input's aria-activedescendant must equal 'autoCompleteJS_result_0'.
After a second ArrowDown, aria-activedescendant must equal 'autoCompleteJS_result_1'.
Pressing Enter should populate the form with the highlighted option's label (e.g., 'Marina Park').
ArrowUp navigation should similarly update aria-activedescendant to the previous option's ID.
